nodes.name: Composite minimization problem (intro)
nodes.statement: \min_{\mathbf{x}\in \mathds{R}^d}~ f(\mathbf{x}) + g(\mathbf{x})
nodes.label: com_min

nodes.name: Finite-sum loss
nodes.statement: f(\mathbf{x}) := \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(\mathbf{x})
nodes.label: finitesum

nodes.name: Proper closed extended real-valued function, domain
nodes.statement: Throughout, $h:\mathds{R}^d \to (-\infty, +\infty]$ denotes an extended real-valued function that is proper and closed, {i.e.}\xspace, its domain $\mathop{\mathrm{dom}} h := \{ \mathbf{x}: h(\mathbf{x}) < +\infty \}$ is nonempty and its sublevel set $\{ \mathbf{x}: h(\mathbf{x}) \leq \alpha \}$ is closed for all $\alpha\in\mathds{R}$.
nodes.statement_short: h is proper and closed: its domain is nonempty and its sublevel sets are closed.

nodes.name: Subdifferential and critical point
nodes.statement: The Frech\'et subdifferential $\hat\partial h$ of $h$ at $\mathbf{x}\in\mathop{\mathrm{dom}} h$ is the set of $\mathbf{u}$ such that \begin{align} \liminf_{\mathbf{z}\neq\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{z}\to\mathbf{x}} \frac{h(\mathbf{z}) - h(\mathbf{x}) - \mathbf{u}^\top(\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x})}{\|\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x}\|} \geq 0, \end{align} while the (limiting) subdifferential $\partial h$ at $\mathbf{x}\in\mathop{\mathrm{dom}} h$ is the ``closure'' of $\hat\partial h$: \begin{align} \{ \mathbf{u}: \exists \mathbf{x}^k \to \mathbf{x}, h(\mathbf{x}^k) \to h(\mathbf{x}), \mathbf{u}^k \in \hat{\partial} h(\mathbf{x}^k), \mathbf{u}^k \to \mathbf{u} \}. \end{align} The critical points of $h$ are $\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} h := \{ \mathbf{x}: \mathbf{0}\in\partial h(\mathbf{x}) \}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fréchet subdifferential via a liminf condition, limiting subdifferential as its closure, critical points where 0 is a subgradient.
nodes.label: def:sub

nodes.name: Frechet subdifferential condition
nodes.statement: \liminf_{\mathbf{z}\neq\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{z}\to\mathbf{x}} \frac{h(\mathbf{z}) - h(\mathbf{x}) - \mathbf{u}^\top(\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x})}{\|\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x}\|} \geq 0,

nodes.name: Limiting subdifferential
nodes.statement: \{ \mathbf{u}: \exists \mathbf{x}^k \to \mathbf{x}, h(\mathbf{x}^k) \to h(\mathbf{x}), \mathbf{u}^k \in \hat{\partial} h(\mathbf{x}^k), \mathbf{u}^k \to \mathbf{u} \}.

nodes.name: Subdifferential coincides with usual notions
nodes.statement: When $h$ is continuously differentiable or convex, the subdifferential $\partial h$ and the set of critical points $\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} h$ coincide with the usual notions.
conclusions: the subdifferential $\partial h$ and the set of critical points $\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} h$ coincide with the usual notions

nodes.name: Nonemptiness of subdifferential of closed functions
nodes.statement: For a closed function $h$, its subdifferential is either nonempty at any point in its domain or the subgradient diverges to some ``direction'' \cite[Corollary 8.10]{vari_ana}.
conclusions: its subdifferential is either nonempty at any point in its domain or the subgradient diverges to some ``direction''

nodes.name: Distance and projection
nodes.statement: The distance function {w.r.t.}\xspace a closed set $\Omega \subseteq \mathds{R}^d$ is defined as: \begin{align} \mathrm{dist}_{\Omega}(\mathbf{x}) := \min_{\mathbf{y}\in\Omega} \|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|, \end{align} while the metric projection onto $\Omega$ is defined as: \begin{align} \proj{\Omega}(\mathbf{x}) := \mathop{\mathrm{argmin}}_{\mathbf{y}\in\Omega} \|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|, \end{align} where $\|\cdot\|$ is the usual Euclidean norm.
nodes.label: def: distance

nodes.name: Distance function
nodes.statement: \mathrm{dist}_{\Omega}(\mathbf{x}) := \min_{\mathbf{y}\in\Omega} \|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|,

nodes.name: Metric projection
nodes.statement: \proj{\Omega}(\mathbf{x}) := \mathop{\mathrm{argmin}}_{\mathbf{y}\in\Omega} \|\mathbf{y}-\mathbf{x}\|,

nodes.name: Projection single-valued iff convex
nodes.statement: Note that $\proj{\Omega}(\mathbf{x})$ is single-valued for all $\mathbf{x}\in\mathds{R}^d$ if and only if $\Omega$ is convex.
conclusions: $\proj{\Omega}(\mathbf{x})$ is single-valued for all $\mathbf{x}\in\mathds{R}^d$ if and only if $\Omega$ is convex

nodes.name: Proximal map
nodes.statement: The proximal map of a closed and proper function $h$ is (with parameter $\eta > 0$): \begin{align} \prox{h}(\mathbf{x}) := \mathop{\mathrm{argmin}}_{\mathbf{z}\in \mathds{R}^d} h(\mathbf{z}) + \tfrac{1}{2\eta}\|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}\|^2. \end{align} Occasionally, we will write $\prox[]{h}$ instead of $\prox[1]{h}$.
nodes.statement_short: prox of h at x with parameter eta: argmin of h(z) + ||z-x||^2/(2 eta).
nodes.label: def:prox_map

nodes.name: Proximal map formula
nodes.statement: \prox{h}(\mathbf{x}) := \mathop{\mathrm{argmin}}_{\mathbf{z}\in \mathds{R}^d} h(\mathbf{z}) + \tfrac{1}{2\eta}\|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}\|^2.

nodes.name: Proximal map of an indicator is the projection
nodes.statement: Clearly, for the indicator function $ h(\mathbf{x}) = \iota_\Omega(\mathbf{x})$, which takes the value 0 for $\mathbf{x}\in \Omega$ and $\infty$ otherwise, its proximal map (with any $\eta > 0$) reduces to the metric projection $\proj{\Omega}$.
conclusions: its proximal map (with any $\eta > 0$) reduces to the metric projection $\proj{\Omega}$

nodes.name: Well-definedness of the proximal map
nodes.statement: If $h$ decreases slower than a quadratic function (in particular, when $h$ is bounded below), then its proximal map is well-defined for all (small) $\eta$ \cite{vari_ana}.
assumptions: $h$ decreases slower than a quadratic function (in particular, when $h$ is bounded below)
conclusions: its proximal map is well-defined for all (small) $\eta$

nodes.name: Proximal map of convex function is single-valued
nodes.statement: If $h$ is convex, then its proximal map is always a singleton while for nonconvex $h$, the proximal map can be set-valued.
conclusions: its proximal map is always a singleton
the proximal map can be set-valued
its proximal map is always a singleton
the proximal map can be set-valued

also_stated_at: Note that for convex functions $g$ the proximal mapping $\prox[\eta]{g}$ is single valued for any $\eta > 0$.

nodes.name: Selection convention for set-valued proximal map
nodes.statement: In the latter case we will also abuse the notation $\prox{h}(\mathbf{x})$ for an arbitrary element from that set.

nodes.name: Nonexpansiveness of the proximal map
nodes.statement: For convex functions, the proximal map is nonexpansive: \begin{align} \forall \mathbf{x}, \forall \mathbf{y}, ~ \|\prox{h}(\mathbf{x}) - \prox{h}(\mathbf{y}) \| \leq \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|, \end{align} while for nonconvex functions this may not hold everywhere.
conclusions: \forall \mathbf{x}, \forall \mathbf{y}, ~ \|\prox{h}(\mathbf{x}) - \prox{h}(\mathbf{y}) \| \leq \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|,

nodes.name: Nonexpansiveness inequality
nodes.statement: \forall \mathbf{x}, \forall \mathbf{y}, ~ \|\prox{h}(\mathbf{x}) - \prox{h}(\mathbf{y}) \| \leq \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|,
nodes.label: eq:ne

nodes.name: proximal gradient algorithm
nodes.statement: The proximal map is the key component of the proximal gradient algorithm \cite{FukushimaMine81} ({a.k.a.}\xspace forward-backward splitting): \begin{align} \forall\,t = 0, 1, \ldots, \quad \mathbf{x}(t+1) = \prox[\eta]{g}\big(\mathbf{x}(t) - \eta \nabla f(\mathbf{x}(t))\big), \end{align} where $\nabla f$ is the (sub)gradient of $f$, and $\eta$ is a suitable step size (that may change with $t$).
input: $\eta$ is a suitable step size (that may change with $t$)
nodes.statement_short: Forward-backward splitting: gradient step on f followed by the proximal map of g.

nodes.name: Proximal gradient iteration
nodes.statement: \forall\,t = 0, 1, \ldots, \quad \mathbf{x}(t+1) = \prox[\eta]{g}\big(\mathbf{x}(t) - \eta \nabla f(\mathbf{x}(t))\big),
nodes.label: eq:pg

nodes.name: Convergence rate of proximal gradient for convex f
nodes.statement: It is known that when $f$ is convex with $L$-Lipschitz continuous gradient and $0 < \eta < 2/L$, then $F_t := f(\mathbf{x}(t))+g(\mathbf{x}(t))$ converges to the minimum at the rate $O(1/t)$ and $\mathbf{x}(t)$ converges to some minimizer $\mathbf{x}^*$.
conclusions: $F_t := f(\mathbf{x}(t))+g(\mathbf{x}(t))$ converges to the minimum at the rate $O(1/t)$
$\mathbf{x}(t)$ converges to some minimizer $\mathbf{x}^*$

nodes.name: Accelerated proximal gradient rate
nodes.statement: Accelerated versions \cite{FISTA,Nesterov13} where $F_t$ converges at the faster rate $O(1/t^2)$ are also well-known.
conclusions: $F_t$ converges at the faster rate $O(1/t^2)$

nodes.name: Convergence of proximal gradient under KL inequality
nodes.statement: Recently, \cite{prox_alter_linear} proved that $\mathbf{x}(t)$ converges to a critical point even for nonconvex $f$ and nonconvex and nonsmooth $g$ as long as together they satisfy a certain K\L\xspace inequality.
assumptions: nonconvex $f$ and nonconvex and nonsmooth $g$ as long as together they satisfy a certain K\L\xspace inequality
conclusions: $\mathbf{x}(t)$ converges to a critical point

nodes.name: Composite minimization problem (P)
nodes.statement: \min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathds{R}^d} F(\mathbf{x}), \quad \mbox{ where } \quad F(\mathbf{x}) = f(\mathbf{x}) + g(\mathbf{x}). \tag{P}
nodes.statement_short: Minimize F = f + g over R^d.
nodes.label: compmin

nodes.name: Model parallel system with p machines
nodes.statement: We consider a \textbf{model} parallel system with $p$ machines in total, and decompose the $d$ model parameters into $p$ disjoint groups.

nodes.name: Block decomposition and partial gradients
nodes.statement: Formally, consider the decomposition $ \mathds{R}^d = \mathds{R}^{d_1} \times \mathds{R}^{d_2} \times\cdots\times\mathds{R}^{d_p}$, and denote $x_i$ and $\nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}): \mathds{R}^d \to \mathds{R}^{d_i}$ as the $i$-th component of $\mathbf{x}$ and $\nabla f(\mathbf{x})$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Split R^d into p blocks; x_i and grad_i f are the i-th block of x and of the gradient.

nodes.name: Local full model on each machine
nodes.statement: The $i$-th machine is responsible for updating the component $x_i\in\mathds{R}^{d_i}$, and for the purpose of evaluating the partial gradient $\nabla_i f(\mathbf{x})$ we assume the $i$-th machine also has access to a local, full model parameter $\mathbf{x}^i\in\mathds{R}^d$.

nodes.name: Bounded Below
nodes.statement: The function $F \!=\! f+g$ is bounded below.
nodes.label: assum:bb

nodes.name: Smooth
nodes.statement:
The gradient $
abla f$ of $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz continuous:  egin{align}  orall \mathbf{x},  orall \mathbf{y}, ~ \| 
abla f(\mathbf{x}) - 
abla f(\mathbf{y}) \| \leq L \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|. \end{align}
nodes.label: assum:smooth

nodes.name: Lipschitz gradient
nodes.statement: \forall \mathbf{x}, \forall \mathbf{y}, ~ \| \nabla f(\mathbf{x}) - \nabla f(\mathbf{y}) \| \leq L \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|.

nodes.name: Separable
nodes.statement: The function $g$ is closed and separable, {i.e.}\xspace, $g(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{i=1}^{p} g_i(x_i)$.
nodes.label: assum:separable

nodes.name: Quadratic upper bound (descent lemma)
nodes.statement: \forall \mathbf{x}, \forall \mathbf{y}, ~f(\mathbf{x}) \leq f(\mathbf{y}) + \langle \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}, \nabla f(\mathbf{y}) \rangle + \tfrac{L}{2} \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|^2.
nodes.label: eq:qb

nodes.name: Separability of the proximal map
nodes.statement: \prox{g}(\mathbf{x}) = \big( \prox{g_1}(x_1),~ \ldots~,~ \prox{g_p}(x_p) \big).

nodes.name: Update operator on machine i
nodes.statement: Then, the update on machine $i$ is defined as: \begin{align} x_i \gets \prox{g_i}(x_i - \eta \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i)). \end{align} That is, machine $i$ computes a partial gradient mapping \cite{Nesterov13} {w.r.t.}\xspace the $i$-th component using the local component $x_i$ and the local full model $\mathbf{x}^i$.
nodes.statement_short: Machine i applies a partial proximal gradient step to its block using its local full model.

nodes.name: Local update rule
nodes.statement: x_i \gets \prox{g_i}(x_i - \eta \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i)).
nodes.label: update_op

nodes.name: Global clock and active clocks
nodes.statement: To define the latter, consider a global clock shared by all machines and denote $T_i$ as the set of active clocks when machine $i$ performs an update.

nodes.name: m-PAPG
nodes.statement: Formally, the $t$-th iteration on machine $i$ can be written as: \begin{equation} \tag{\textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace} \left\{ \begin{aligned} \forall i,~ x_i(t+1) &= \begin{cases} x_i(t), & t \not\in T_i \\ \prox{g_i}(x_i(t) - \eta \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t))), & t \in T_i \end{cases} , \\ \mbox{(local) } \quad \mathbf{x}^i(t) &= \big( x_1(\tau_1^i(t)),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(\tau_p^i(t)) \big), \\ \mbox{(global)}\quad \mathbf{x}(t) &= \big( x_1(t),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(t) \big). \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation} That is, machine $i$ only performs its update operator at its active clocks. The local full model $\mathbf{x}^i(t)$ assembles all components from other machines, and is possibly a delayed version of the global model $\mathbf{x}(t)$, which assembles the most up-to-date component in each machine. Note that the global model is introduced for our analysis, and is not accessible in a real implementation. More specifically, $\tau_j^i(t) \leq t$ models the communication delay among machines: when machine $i$ conducts its $t$-th update it only has access to $x_j(\tau_j^i(t))$, a delayed version of the component $x_j(t)$ on the $j$-th machine. We refer to the above algorithm as \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace (for \textbf{m}odel parallel, \textbf{P}artially \textbf{A}synchronous, \textbf{P}roximal \textbf{G}radient).
input: $\tau_j^i(t) \leq t$ models the communication delay among machines
nodes.statement_short: Model-parallel partially asynchronous proximal gradient: each machine updates its block at its active clocks using a delayed local copy of the model.

nodes.name: m-PAPG iteration
nodes.statement: \tag{\textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace} \left\{ \begin{aligned} \forall i,~ x_i(t+1) &= \begin{cases} x_i(t), & t \not\in T_i \\ \prox{g_i}(x_i(t) - \eta \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t))), & t \in T_i \end{cases} , \\ \mbox{(local) } \quad \mathbf{x}^i(t) &= \big( x_1(\tau_1^i(t)),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(\tau_p^i(t)) \big), \\ \mbox{(global)}\quad \mathbf{x}(t) &= \big( x_1(t),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(t) \big). \end{aligned} \right.
nodes.label: mspg_formulation

nodes.name: Block update at active clocks
nodes.statement: x_i(t+1) &= \begin{cases} x_i(t), & t \not\in T_i \\ \prox{g_i}(x_i(t) - \eta \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t))), & t \in T_i \end{cases}
nodes.statement_short: Update block i by a partial prox-gradient step if t is active, else keep it.

nodes.name: Assemble delayed local model
nodes.statement: \mbox{(local) } \quad \mathbf{x}^i(t) &= \big( x_1(\tau_1^i(t)),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(\tau_p^i(t)) \big)
nodes.statement_short: Form the local full model from delayed copies of all blocks.

nodes.name: Assemble global model
nodes.statement: \mbox{(global)}\quad \mathbf{x}(t) &= \big( x_1(t),~ \ldots~,~ x_p(t) \big)
nodes.statement_short: Form the global model from the latest blocks (for analysis only).

nodes.name: Bounded Delay
nodes.statement: $\exists s \in \mathds{N}, ~\forall i, \forall j, \forall t, ~0 \leq t-\tau_j^i(t) \leq s$, $\tau_i^i(t) \equiv t$.
nodes.label: assum:delay

nodes.name: Frequent Update
nodes.statement: $\exists s \in \mathds{N}, ~\forall i, \forall t, T_i \cap \{t, t+1, \cdots, t+s\} \ne \emptyset$.
nodes.label: assum:skip

nodes.name: Synchronous special case
nodes.statement: Clearly, when $s = 0$ ({i.e.}\xspace, no delay), \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace reduces to the fully synchronous, model parallel proximal gradient algorithm.

nodes.name: Positive part
nodes.statement: Recall that $(t)_+ = \max\{t, 0\}$ is the positive part of $t$.

nodes.name: Inconsistency bound between local and global models
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:delay} hold, then the global model $\mathbf{x}(t)$ and the local models $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ satisfy: \begin{align} \forall i=1,\cdots,p, ~~ \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \| \\ \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|. \end{align}
conclusions: \forall i=1,\cdots,p, ~~ \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|
\|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|.
nodes.statement_short: Under bounded delay, local-global model gaps and local model increments are bounded by sums of recent global increments.
nodes.label: thm:incon

nodes.name: Local-global inconsistency bound
nodes.statement: \forall i=1,\cdots,p, ~~ \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|

nodes.name: Local model increment bound
nodes.statement: \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| \leq \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (inconsistency bound)
nodes.statement: Indeed, by the definitions in \eqref{mspg_formulation}: \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(t) - x_j(\tau_j^i(t)) \|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = \tau_j^i(t)}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &{\leq} \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &=\sum_{j=1}^p \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\|x_j(k'+1) - x_j(k') \| \\ &=\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\|x_j(k'+1) - x_j(k') \| \\ &{\leq}\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|\|\mathbf{x}(k'+1) - \mathbf{x}(k') \| \\ &= \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} where the first inequality is due to the triangle inequality; the second inequality is due to \Cref{assum:delay}; and the last inequality follows from the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Similarly, \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}^{i}(t) - \mathbf{x}^{i}(t+1)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t)) - x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t+1))\|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = \tau_j^i(t)}^{\tau_j^i(t+1)-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} and the rest of the proof is completely similar to the previous case.
nodes.statement_short: Expand blockwise, apply triangle inequality, bounded delay and Cauchy-Schwarz; the second bound is analogous.

nodes.name: Bound local-global gap
nodes.statement: Indeed, by the definitions in \eqref{mspg_formulation}: \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(t) - x_j(\tau_j^i(t)) \|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = \tau_j^i(t)}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &{\leq} \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &=\sum_{j=1}^p \sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\|x_j(k'+1) - x_j(k') \| \\ &=\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\|x_j(k'+1) - x_j(k') \| \\ &{\leq}\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \sum_{k' = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|\|\mathbf{x}(k'+1) - \mathbf{x}(k') \| \\ &= \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} where the first inequality is due to the triangle inequality; the second inequality is due to \Cref{assum:delay}; and the last inequality follows from the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Bound ||x(t)-x^i(t)|| via triangle inequality, bounded delay and Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Bound local increment similarly
nodes.statement: Similarly, \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}^{i}(t) - \mathbf{x}^{i}(t+1)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t)) - x_j(\tau_{j}^i(t+1))\|^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = \tau_j^i(t)}^{\tau_j^i(t+1)-1} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2 \\ &\leq \sum_{j=1}^p \left(\sum_{k = (t-s)_+}^{t} \|x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|\right)^2, \end{align*} and the rest of the proof is completely similar to the previous case.
nodes.statement_short: The local increment bound follows by the same argument.

nodes.name: Square summability of m-PAPG iterates
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:bb,assum:smooth,assum:separable,assum:delay,assum:skip} hold. If the step size $\eta \in \left(0, \frac{1}{L(1+2\sqrt{p}s)}\right)$, then the sequence generated by \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace is square summable, {i.e.}\xspace \begin{align} \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|^2 < \infty. \end{align} In particular, $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| = 0$ and $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| = 0$.
conclusions: the sequence generated by \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace is square summable
$\lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| = 0$ and  $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| = 0$
nodes.statement_short: With small enough step size, m-PAPG successive differences are square summable and local-global inconsistency vanishes.
nodes.label: thm:limitcon

nodes.name: Square summability
nodes.statement: \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|^2 < \infty.
nodes.label: sq_summable

nodes.name: Remark on the step size bound
nodes.statement: Our bound on the step size $\eta$ is natural: If $s = 0$, {i.e.}\xspace, there is no asynchronism then we recover the standard step size rule $\eta < 1/L$ (we can increase $\eta$ by another factor of 2, had convexity on $g$ been assumed). As staleness $s$ increases, we need a smaller step size to ``damp'' the system to still ensure convergence. The factor $\sqrt{p}$ is another measurement of the degree of ``dependency'' among worker machines: Indeed, we can reduce $\sqrt{p}$ to $\sqrt{\sum_i L_i^2} / L$, where $L_i$ is the Lipschitz constant of $\nabla_i f$ ({cf.}\xspace \eqref{eq:Lip}).
nodes.statement_short: The step size recovers 1/L when s=0, shrinks with staleness; sqrt(p) can be replaced by a ratio of blockwise Lipschitz constants.

nodes.statement: It is clear from \Cref{thm:limitcon} that $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ and $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}, i=1, \ldots, p$, share the same set of limit points, and we need to show that any limit point of $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ is also a critical point of $F$.
nodes.statement_short: Shared limit points follow from Theorem 1; it remains to show criticality.

nodes.name: Criterion via subdifferential definition
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{x}^*$ be a limit point of $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$. By \Cref{def:sub} it suffices to exhibit a sequence $\mathbf{x}(k)$ satisfying\footnote{Technically, from \Cref{def:sub} we should have the Frech\'et subdifferential $\hat{\partial} F$ in \cref{crit_want}, however, a standard argument allows us to use the more convenient subdifferential \cite[Proposition 8.7]{vari_ana}.} \begin{align} \mathbf{x}(k) \to \mathbf{x}^*, ~ F(\mathbf{x}(k)) \to F(\mathbf{x}^*), ~ \mathbf{0} \leftarrow \mathbf{u}(k) \in \partial F(\mathbf{x}(k)). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to find a sequence converging with function values and vanishing subgradients.

nodes.name: Construct subgradients at active clocks
nodes.statement: Let us first construct the subgradient sequence $\mathbf{u}(k)$. Consider machine $i$ and any $\hat t \in T_i$, the optimality condition of \cref{update_exp} gives \begin{flalign} u_i( \hat t+1) := -\tfrac{1}{\eta} \left[x_i(\hat t+1) - x_i(\hat t) + \eta \nabla_{i} f\big(\mathbf{x}^i(\hat t)\big)\right] \in \partial g_i(x_i( \hat t+1)). \end{flalign}
nodes.statement_short: Prox optimality yields u_i in the subdifferential of g_i.

It then follows that  egin{flalign} \|u_i( \hat t+1) & + 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}( \hat t+1))\| 
onumber\ &\leq \|u_i( \hat t+1) + 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}( \hat t ))\| + \|
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}( \hat t+1)) - 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}(\hat t))\| 
onumber\ &\overset{\mathrm{(i)}}{\le} \left\| 	frac{1}{\eta} \left[ x_i( \hat t+1) - x_i(\hat t) ight] + 
abla_{i} f ig(\mathbf{x}^{i}(\hat t) ig) - 
abla_{i} f ig(\mathbf{x}(\hat t) ig) ight\| + L\|\mathbf{x}(\hat t+1) - \mathbf{x}(\hat t)\|

nodes.statement: Combining the two cases in \cref{sub_zero_1} and \cref{sub_zero_2} we have for all $t$: \begin{align} \| \mathbf{u}(t+1) + \nabla f(\mathbf{x}(t+1))\| \leq (\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L) {\sum_{k = (t-2s)_+}^t} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|, \end{align} where $\mathbf{u}(t+1) = \big( u_1(t+1),~ \ldots~,~ u_p(t+1) \big) \in \partial g (\mathbf{x}(t+1))$, and the factor $\sqrt{p} \geq 1$ is artificially introduced for the convenience of subsequent analysis.

nodes.statement: Since each machine updates at least once during $[t_m-s, t_m]$, let $\hat t_m$ be the largest element of $[t_m-s, t_m] \cap T_i$. nodes.statement_short: By the subdifferential definition, x* is critical.

conclusions: A prototypic convex function $F$ satisfying \eqref{eq:eb} is the following:

nodes.name: Prototype composite function f(Ax)+g(x)
nodes.statement: F(\mathbf{x}) = f(A\mathbf{x}) + g(\mathbf{x}),
nodes.label: eq:prototype

nodes.name: Error bound equivalent to restricted strong convexity and quadratic growth
nodes.statement: In fact, for convex functions $F$ taking such form, the error bound condition in \cref{eq:eb} is recently shown to be equivalent to the following conditions \cite{DrusvyatskiyLewis16,Zhang2016}: \begin{align*} \text{Restricted strong convexity}: ~ &\inner{ \mathbf{x} - \prox[]{g}(\mathbf{x})}{\mathbf{x} - \proj{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}(\mathbf{x})} \ge \mu \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}^2(\mathbf{x}), \\ \text{Quadratic growth}: ~ &F(\mathbf{x}) - F^* \ge \mu \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}^2(\mathbf{x}), \end{align*} where $F^*$ is the minimum value of $F$ and $\mu>0$ is a constant.
conclusions: the error bound condition in \cref{eq:eb} is recently shown to be equivalent to the following conditions

nodes.name: Restricted strong convexity and quadratic growth
nodes.statement: \text{Restricted strong convexity}: ~ &\inner{ \mathbf{x} - \prox[]{g}(\mathbf{x})}{\mathbf{x} - \proj{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}(\mathbf{x})} \ge \mu \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}^2(\mathbf{x}), \\ \text{Quadratic growth}: ~ &F(\mathbf{x}) - F^* \ge \mu \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}^2(\mathbf{x}),
nodes.label: eq: rsc

nodes.name: Error bound for a nonconvex example
nodes.statement: In general, the error bound condition in \cref{eq:eb} is not exclusive to convex functions. For instance, it holds for $f(\mathbf{x})= \tfrac{1}{2}\|\mathbf{x}\|^2$ and any function $g$ that has a unique global minimizer at $0$ (such as the cardinality function $g(\mathbf{x}) = \|\mathbf{x}\|_0$).

nodes.name: Progress quantities A(t) and B(t)
nodes.statement: We define the following nonnegative quantities that measure the progress of \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace: \begin{align} A(t) &:= F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^*, ~ F^* :=\inf_{\mathbf{x}} F(\mathbf{x}), \\ B(t) &:= \sum_{k=(t-s-1)_+}^{t-1} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\|^2, \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: A(t) is the objective gap, B(t) the sum of squared increments over the last s+1 steps.

nodes.name: Objective gap A(t)
nodes.statement: A(t) &:= F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^*, ~ F^* :=\inf_{\mathbf{x}} F(\mathbf{x}),

nodes.name: Recursive gap relations under error bound
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:bb,assum:smooth,assum:separable,assum:delay,assum:skip,assum:convex,assum:eb} hold. Then, we have \begin{align*} & A(t+s+1) \le A(t) - \tfrac{1}{2}(\tfrac{1}{\eta} - L - 2sL \sqrt{p}) B(t+s+1) + \tfrac{1}{2}sL\sqrt{p} B(t) \\ & 0 \le A(t+s+1) \le a_\eta B(t+s+1) + b B(t), \end{align*} where $a_\eta$ and $b$ are given in \eqref{eq:ab} below.
conclusions: A(t+s+1) \le A(t) - \tfrac{1}{2}(\tfrac{1}{\eta} - L - 2sL \sqrt{p}) B(t+s+1) + \tfrac{1}{2}sL\sqrt{p} B(t)
0 \le A(t+s+1) \le a_\eta B(t+s+1) + b B(t),
nodes.statement_short: Over s+1 steps the gap A decreases by a multiple of B, and A is bounded by a combination of consecutive B's.
nodes.label: lemma: EB_2

nodes.name: Proof of recursive gap relations
nodes.statement:
The first inequality is obtained by summing the inequality \cref{eq: progress} over $t, t+1, \cdots, t+s$. So we need only prove the second inequality. Let us introduce some notations to simplify the proof. For each machine $i$ let $t_i$ be the largest clock in $[t, t+s] \cap T_i$, and denote  egin{align} \mathbf{z} &=  ig(x_1(t_1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t_p) ig) \ \mathbf{z}^+ &=  ig(x_1(t_1+1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t_p+1) ig) =  ig(x_1(t+s+1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t+s+1) ig), \end{align} where the last equality is due to the maximality of each $t_i$. From the optimality condition of the proximal map $z^+_i = \prox{g_i}(z_i - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t_i)))$ we deduce  egin{align} \eta^{-1} (z_i - z_i^+) - 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i)) \in \partial g_i (z_i^+). \end{align} Since the gradient of $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz continuous and the function $g$ is convex, we obtain  egin{align*} f(\mathbf{z}^+) - f( ar{\mathbf{z}}) &\le \sum_{i=1}^p \langle z^+_i -  ar z_i, 
abla_i f( ar{\mathbf{z}})angle +  rac{L}{2} \|\mathbf{z}^+ -  ar{\mathbf{z}}\|^2, \ g(\mathbf{z}^+) - g( ar{\mathbf{z}}) &\le \sum_{i=1}^p \langle z^+_i -  ar z_i, \eta^{-1} (z_i - z_i^+) - 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i)) angle, \end{align*} where we define $ ar {\mathbf{z}} := \proj{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}(\mathbf{z})$, {i.e.}\xspace, the projection of $\mathbf{z}$ onto the set of critical points of $F$, and the last inequality follows from \cref{eq:subgrad}. Adding up the above two inequalities we obtain  egin{align*} F(&\mathbf{z}^+) - F^* - 	frac{L}{2} \|\mathbf{z}^+ -  ar{\mathbf{z}}\|^2 \le \sum_{i=1}^p \langle z^+_i -  ar z_i,

abla f$. Using again the triangle inequality we obtain from the above inequality that  egin{align} F(\mathbf{z}^+) - F^* &\le (L+4)\| ar{\mathbf{z}} - \mathbf{z}\|^2 + (L+4+	frac{4}{\eta^{2}}) \|\mathbf{z}^+ - \mathbf{z}\|^2 + 4L^2\sum_{i=1}^{p} \|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) - \mathbf{z}\|^2 
onumber\ 
onumber&\overset{\mathrm{(i)}}{=} (L\!+\!4)\| ar{\mathbf{z}} \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2 \!+\! \sum_{i=1}^{p} [(L\!+\!4\!+\!	frac{4}{\eta^{2}})\|x_i(t_i\!+\!1) \!-\! x_i(t_i)\|^2 \!+\! 4L^2\|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2],\ &\overset{\mathrm{(ii)}}{\leq} (L\!+\!4)\| ar{\mathbf{z}} \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2 + (L\!+\!4\!+\!	frac{4}{\eta^{2}}) B(t+s+1) + 4L^2\sum_{i=1}^{p} \|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2, \end{align} where (i) is due to our definition of $\mathbf{z}$ and $\mathbf{z}^+$ in \eqref{eq:z} and \eqref{eq:z2}, and (ii) is due to the fact that $t_i \in [t, t+s]$ for all $i$. We next bound the terms $\| ar{\mathbf{z}} - \mathbf{z}\|^2$ and $\|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2$. First, note that  egin{align*} \| x_i(t_i+1) - x_i(t_i)\| &= \|\prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i))) - x_i(t_i)\| \ &\ge \|\prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{z})) - x_i(t_i)\| \ &\quad - \|\prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta

abla f$. Rearranging the above inequality and summing over all $i$, we obtain  egin{align}

onumber \|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}^i(t_i)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(t_j) - x_j (	au_j^i (t_i))\|^2 \ &= \sum_{j=1}^p \Big\|\sum_{k = \min\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \} }^{\max\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \}-1} x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \Big\|^2 
onumber\ &\le \sum_{j=1}^p \Big[\sum_{k = \min\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \} }^{\max\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \}-1} \| x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \| \Big]^2

nodes.name: First inequality and reduction
nodes.statement: The first inequality is obtained by summing the inequality \cref{eq: progress} over $t, t+1, \cdots, t+s$. So we need only prove the second inequality.
nodes.statement_short: First inequality by summing (23); only the second remains.

nodes.name: Introduce z and z+
nodes.statement: Let us introduce some notations to simplify the proof. For each machine $i$ let $t_i$ be the largest clock in $[t, t+s] \cap T_i$, and denote \begin{align} \mathbf{z} &= \big(x_1(t_1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t_p)\big) \\ \mathbf{z}^+ &= \big(x_1(t_1+1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t_p+1)\big) = \big(x_1(t+s+1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t+s+1)\big), \end{align} where the last equality is due to the maximality of each $t_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Define z, z+ from the last active clocks in [t, t+s].

nodes.name: Prox optimality subgradient
nodes.statement: From the optimality condition of the proximal map $z^+_i = \prox{g_i}(z_i - \eta \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t_i)))$ we deduce \begin{align} \eta^{-1} (z_i - z_i^+) - \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i)) \in \partial g_i (z_i^+). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Optimality of the prox step gives a subgradient of g_i at z_i^+.

nodes.name: Bounds for f and g
nodes.statement: Since the gradient of $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz continuous and the function $g$ is convex, we obtain \begin{align*} f(\mathbf{z}^+) - f(\bar{\mathbf{z}}) &\le \sum_{i=1}^p \langle z^+_i - \bar z_i, \nabla_i f(\bar{\mathbf{z}})\rangle + \frac{L}{2} \|\mathbf{z}^+ - \bar{\mathbf{z}}\|^2, \\ g(\mathbf{z}^+) - g(\bar{\mathbf{z}}) &\le \sum_{i=1}^p \langle z^+_i - \bar z_i, \eta^{-1} (z_i - z_i^+) - \nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i)) \rangle, \end{align*} where we define $\bar {\mathbf{z}} := \proj{\mathop{\mathrm{crit}} F}(\mathbf{z})$, {i.e.}\xspace, the projection of $\mathbf{z}$ onto the set of critical points of $F$, and the last inequality follows from \cref{eq:subgrad}.
nodes.statement_short: Descent lemma for f and convexity of g relative to the projection of z on crit F.

nodes.name: Add and estimate
nodes.statement:
Adding up the above two inequalities we obtain  egin{align*} F(&\mathbf{z}^+) - F^* - 	frac{L}{2} \|\mathbf{z}^+ -  ar{\mathbf{z}}\|^2 \le \sum_{i=1}^p \langle z^+_i -  ar z_i, 
abla_i f( ar{\mathbf{z}}) + \eta^{-1} (z_i - z_i^+) - 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i))angle \ &\overset{\mathrm{(i)}}{\le} \sum_{i=1}^{p} [\|z_i^+ - z_i\| + \|z_i -  ar z_i\|] [\|
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i)) - 
abla_i f( ar{\mathbf{z}})\| + \eta^{-1} \|z_i - z_i^+\|] \ &\overset{\mathrm{(ii)}}{\le} \sum_{i=1}^{p} 4\left[ \|z_i^+ - z_i\|^2 + \|z_i -  ar z_i\|^2 + \eta^{-2} \|z_i^+ - z_i\|^2 + \|
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i)) - 
abla_i f( ar{\mathbf{z}})\|^2 ight] \ &\le 4\left[ \| ar{\mathbf{z}} - \mathbf{z}\|^2 + (1+\eta^{-2}) \|\mathbf{z}^+ - \mathbf{z}\|^2 + \sum_{i=1}^{p} L^2 \|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) -  ar{\mathbf{z}}\|^2 ight], \end{align*} where (i) is due to the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and the triangle inequality, (ii) is due to the elementary inequality $(a+b)(c+d) \leq 4(a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2)$, and the last inequality is due to the $L$-Lipschitz continuity of $
abla f$.
nodes.statement_short: Add the bounds; Cauchy-Schwarz, triangle and elementary inequalities.

nodes.name: Gap bound in terms of B
nodes.statement: Using again the triangle inequality we obtain from the above inequality that \begin{align} F(\mathbf{z}^+) - F^* &\le (L+4)\|\bar{\mathbf{z}} - \mathbf{z}\|^2 + (L+4+\tfrac{4}{\eta^{2}}) \|\mathbf{z}^+ - \mathbf{z}\|^2 + 4L^2\sum_{i=1}^{p} \|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) - \mathbf{z}\|^2 \nonumber\\ \nonumber&\overset{\mathrm{(i)}}{=} (L\!+\!4)\|\bar{\mathbf{z}} \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2 \!+\! \sum_{i=1}^{p} [(L\!+\!4\!+\!\tfrac{4}{\eta^{2}})\|x_i(t_i\!+\!1) \!-\! x_i(t_i)\|^2 \!+\! 4L^2\|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2],\\ &\overset{\mathrm{(ii)}}{\leq} (L\!+\!4)\|\bar{\mathbf{z}} \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2 + (L\!+\!4\!+\!\tfrac{4}{\eta^{2}}) B(t+s+1) + 4L^2\sum_{i=1}^{p} \|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2, \end{align} where (i) is due to our definition of $\mathbf{z}$ and $\mathbf{z}^+$ in \eqref{eq:z} and \eqref{eq:z2}, and (ii) is due to the fact that $t_i \in [t, t+s]$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound F(z+)-F* by distance to crit F, B(t+s+1) and local-model gaps.

nodes.name: Lower bound on block increments
nodes.statement:
We next bound the terms $\| ar{\mathbf{z}} - \mathbf{z}\|^2$ and $\|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2$. First, note that  egin{align*} \| x_i(t_i+1) - x_i(t_i)\| &= \|\prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i))) - x_i(t_i)\| \ &\ge \|\prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{z})) - x_i(t_i)\| \ &\quad - \|\prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i (t_i))) - \prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{z})) \| \ &\overset{\mathrm{(i)}}{\ge} \|\prox{g_i}(x_i(t_i) - \eta 
abla_i f(\mathbf{z})) - x_i(t_i)\| - \eta L \|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}^i(t_i)\|, \end{align*} where (i) follows from the non-expansiveness of $\prox{g}$ (recall that $g$ is convex) and the $L$-Lipschitz continuity of $
abla f$.
nodes.statement_short: Nonexpansiveness of prox compares stale and fresh prox steps.

nodes.name: Bound prox residual at z
nodes.statement: Rearranging the above inequality and summing over all $i$, we obtain \begin{align} \nonumber \|\prox{g}(\mathbf{z}- \eta \nabla f(\mathbf{z})) - \mathbf{z}\|^2 &\le \sum_{i=1}^p \left[\| x_i(t_i+1) - x_i(t_i)\| + \eta L \|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}^i(t_i)\| \right]^2 \\ &\le 2\sum_{i=1}^p \left[\| x_i(t_i+1) - x_i(t_i)\||^2 + \eta^2 L^2 \|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}^i(t_i)\|^2 \right]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Sum over blocks to bound the prox-gradient residual at z.

nodes.name: Bound local-model gaps
nodes.statement:
The last term $\|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}^i(t_i)\|^2$ can be further bounded as follows:  egin{align} 
onumber \|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}^i(t_i)\|^2 &= \sum_{j=1}^p \|x_j(t_j) - x_j (	au_j^i (t_i))\|^2 \ &= \sum_{j=1}^p \Big\|\sum_{k = \min\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \} }^{\max\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \}-1} x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \Big\|^2 
onumber\ &\le \sum_{j=1}^p \Big[\sum_{k = \min\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \} }^{\max\{ t_j, 	au_j^i(t_i) \}-1} \| x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \| \Big]^2 
onumber\ &\overset{\mathrm{(i)}}{\le} \sum_{j=1}^p 2s \sum_{k= t-s}^{t+s-1} \| x_j(k+1) - x_j(k) \|^2 
onumber\ 
onumber &= 2s \sum_{k=t-s}^{t+s-1} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\|^2 \ & \leq 2s [B(t) + B(t+s+1)], \end{align} where (i) is due to the fact that $t_j \in [t, t+s]$ and $	au_j^i(t_i) \in [t-s, t+s]$.
nodes.statement_short: Gap between z and local models bounded by 2s(B(t)+B(t+s+1)).

nodes.name: Combine residual bounds
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:proxb} and \eqref{eq:diff} we obtain \begin{align} \|\prox{g}(\mathbf{z} - \eta \nabla f(\mathbf{z})) &- \mathbf{z}\|^2 \leq 2 B(t+s+1) + 4ps\eta^2 L^2 [B(t) + B(t+s+1)]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Residual at z bounded by B terms.

nodes.name: Apply error bound
nodes.statement:
Thanks to \Cref{thm:limitcon}, we know for $t$ sufficiently large, $\|\prox{g}(\mathbf{z} \!-\! \eta 
abla f(\mathbf{z})) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\| \leq \eta\delta$. Since the function $\eta \mapsto  rac{1}{\eta}\|\prox{g}(\mathbf{z} \!-\! \eta 
abla f(\mathbf{z})) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|$ is monotonically decreasing \cite{Sra12}, we can apply the error bound condition in \Cref{assum:eb} for $\eta < 1$ and $t$ sufficiently large, and obtain  egin{align} \| ar{\mathbf{z}} - \mathbf{z}\|^2 \le \kappa \|\mathbf{z} - \prox[]{g}(\mathbf{z} - 
abla f(\mathbf{z}))\|^2 \le \kappa \eta^{-2} \|\mathbf{z} - \prox{g}(\mathbf{z} - \eta
abla f(\mathbf{z}))\|^2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: For large t the residual is small, so the error bound applies (with monotonicity in eta).

nodes.name: Conclude second inequality
nodes.statement: Finally, combining \eqref{eq:Fgap}, \eqref{eq:diff}, \eqref{eq:pb} and \eqref{eq:projdist} we arrive at: \begin{align} \nonumber F(\mathbf{x}(t\!+\!s\!+\!1)) - F^* &= F(\mathbf{z}^+) - F^* \\ \nonumber&\le (L\!+\!4)\|\bar{\mathbf{z}} \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2 + (L\!+\!4\!+\!\tfrac{4}{\eta^{2}}) B(t\!+\!s\!+\!1) + 4L^2\sum_{i=1}^{p} \|\mathbf{x}^i (t_i) \!-\! \mathbf{z}\|^2,\\ &\le a_\eta B(t+s+1) + b B(t), \end{align} where the coefficients are \begin{align} a_\eta &= L+4+8psL^2 + 4ps\kappa L^2(L+4) + \tfrac{2}{\eta^2}(2+4\kappa+\kappa L), \\ b &= 8psL^2+4ps\kappa L^2(L+4). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Combine all bounds to get A(t+s+1) <= a_eta B(t+s+1) + b B(t).

nodes.name: Definition of z
nodes.statement: \mathbf{z} &= \big(x_1(t_1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t_p)\big)
nodes.label: eq:z

nodes.name: Definition of z+
nodes.statement: \mathbf{z}^+ &= \big(x_1(t_1+1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t_p+1)\big) = \big(x_1(t+s+1), ~\ldots~, x_p(t+s+1)\big),
nodes.label: eq:z2

nodes.name: Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega\subset \mathrm{dom} h$ be a compact set on which the function $h$ is a constant. We say that $h$ satisfies the K\L\xspace property if there exist $\varepsilon, \lambda >0$ such that for all $\bar{\mathbf{x}} \in \Omega$ and all $\mathbf{x}\in \{\mathbf{z}\in \mathds{R}^d : \mathrm{dist}_\Omega(\mathbf{z})<\varepsilon\}\cap [\mathbf{z}: h(\bar{\mathbf{x}}) < h(\mathbf{z}) <h(\bar{\mathbf{x}}) + \lambda]$, it holds that \begin{align} \varphi'(h(\mathbf{x}) - h(\bar{\mathbf{x}})) \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\partial h(\mathbf{x})}(\mathbf{0}) \ge 1, \end{align} where the function $\varphi: [0,\lambda) \to \mathds{R}_+, 0\mapsto 0$, is continuous, concave, and has continuous and positive derivative $\varphi'$ on $(0,\lambda)$.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform KL: near a compact level set, phi'(h(x)-h(xbar)) times the subgradient distance is at least 1.
nodes.label: def:KL

nodes.name: KL inequality
nodes.statement: \varphi'(h(\mathbf{x}) - h(\bar{\mathbf{x}})) \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\partial h(\mathbf{x})}(\mathbf{0}) \ge 1,

nodes.name: Sufficient decrease inequality

nodes.name: Descent algorithms satisfy sufficient decrease

nodes.name: Finite Length
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:bb,assum:smooth,assum:separable,assum:delay,assum:skip,assum:sd} hold for \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace, and let $F$ satisfy the K\L\xspace property in \Cref{def:KL}. Then, with step size $\eta \in \left(0, \frac{1}{L(1+2\sqrt{p}s)}\right)$, every bounded sequence $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ generated by \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace satisfies \begin{flalign} \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| < \infty,\\ \forall i = 1, \ldots ,p, ~ \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| < \infty. \end{flalign} Furthermore, $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ and $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ converge to the same critical point of $F$.
conclusions: \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| < \infty,
\forall i = 1, \ldots ,p, ~ \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| < \infty.
$\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ and $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ converge to the same critical point of $F$
nodes.statement_short: Under KL and sufficient decrease, bounded m-PAPG sequences have finite length and converge to one critical point.
nodes.label: thm:finite

nodes.name: Global finite length
nodes.statement: \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| < \infty,
nodes.label: global_finite

nodes.name: Local finite length
nodes.statement: \forall i = 1, \ldots ,p, ~ \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| < \infty.

nodes.name: Proof of Finite Length
nodes.statement:
We first show that \cref{global_finite} implies \cref{local_finite}. Indeed, recall from \eqref{eq:local_diff}:  egin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\|. \end{align*} Therefore, summing for $t=0, 1, \cdots, n$ gives  egin{align*} \sum_{t=0}^n \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{t=0}^n \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \ &\leq (2s+1) \sum_{t=0}^n \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|. \end{align*} The claim then follows by letting $n$ tend to infinity. By \Cref{thm:limitcon}, the limit points of $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ and $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ coincide and are critical points of $F$. Thus, the only thing left to prove is the finite length property in \cref{global_finite}. By \Cref{assum:sd} and \Cref{assum:bb}, the objective value $F(\mathbf{x}(t))$ decreases to a finite limit $F^*$. Since $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ is assumed to be bounded, the set of its limit points $\Omega$ is nonempty and compact. Summing \cref{usc} over all $i$ and set $\mathbf{z} \in \Omega$, we obtain \[ g(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) \le g(\mathbf{z}) -  rac{1}{2\eta} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|^2 - \sum_{i=1}^{p}\inner{
abla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t))}{\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)}. \] Note that $\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t) 	o 0$. Also, since $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ is bounded and $\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)	o 0$ for all $i$, $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ are all bounded. we then take limsup on both sides and obtain that $\limsup_{t	o\infty} g(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) \le g(\mathbf{z})$. Together with the closedness of $g$ we further obtain that $\lim_{t	o\infty} g(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) = g(\mathbf{z})$. Note that $f$ is continuous, we thus conclude that $\lim_{t	o\infty} F(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) = F(\mathbf{z})$ for all $\mathbf{z}\in \Omega$. Note that $F(\mathbf{x}(t)) \downarrow F^*$. Thus for all $\mathbf{x}^* \in \Omega$, we have $F(\mathbf{x}^*) \equiv F^*$. Now fix $\varepsilon > 0$. Since $\Omega$ is compact, for $t$ sufficiently large we have $\mathrm{dist}_{\Omega}(\mathbf{x}(t)) \leq \varepsilon$. We now have all ingredients to apply the K\L\xspace inequality in \Cref{def:KL}: for all sufficiently large $t$,  egin{flalign} \varphi' ig(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^* ig) \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0}) \ge 1. \end{flalign} Since $\varphi$ is concave, we obtain  egin{flalign} \Delta_{t,t+1} &:= \varphi ig(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^* ig) - \varphi ig(F(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) - F^* ig) 
onumber\ &\ge \varphi' ig(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^* ig)  ig(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) -F(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) ig) 
onumber\ &\ovset{(i)}{\ge}  rac{\alpha \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t) \|^2}{\mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0})}, \end{flalign} where (i) follows from \Cref{assum:sd} and \cref{uKL}. It is clear that the function $\varphi$ (composed with $F$) serves as a Lyapunov function. Using the elementary inequality $2\sqrt{ab} \le a + b$ we obtain from \cref{Lyapunov} that for $t$ sufficiently large,  egin{flalign*} 2\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \le 	frac{\delta}{\alpha} \Delta_{t,t+1} + 	frac{1}{\delta}\mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0}), \end{flalign*} where $\delta > 0$ will be specified later. Recalling the bound for $\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))$ in \cref{subdiff_bound}, and summing over $t$ from $m$ (sufficiently large) to $n$ gives:  egin{flalign*} 2\sum_{t=m}^{n}&\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \le \sum_{t=m}^{n}  rac{\delta}{\alpha} \Delta_{t, t+1} + \sum_{t=m}^{n}  rac{1}{\delta} \mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0}) \ &\ovset{(i)}{\le}  rac{\delta}{\alpha} \varphi ig(F(\mathbf{x}(m)) - F^* ig) + \sum_{t=m}^{n}  rac{\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L}{\delta} \sum_{k = (t-2s)_+}^t \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \| \ &\le  rac{\delta}{\alpha} \varphi ig(F(\mathbf{x}(m)) - F^* ig) +  rac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\delta} \sum_{k=(m-2s)_+}^{m-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \| \ &\qquad\qquad \qquad\qquad +  rac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\delta} \sum_{t=m}^{n} \| \mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t) \|, \end{flalign*} where (i) is due to \cref{subdiff_bound}. Setting $\delta = (2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)$ and rearranging gives  egin{flalign*} \sum_{t=m}^{n}\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| &\le  rac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\alpha} \varphi ig(F(\mathbf{x}(m)) - F^* ig) \ &\quad+ \sum_{k=(m-2s)_+}^{m-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|. \end{flalign*} Since the right-hand side is finite, let $n$ tend to infinity completes the proof for \cref{global_finite}.
nodes.statement_short: KL-based Lyapunov argument: concavity of phi with sufficient decrease and the subdifferential bound give summable increments. Key step: choosing delta to absorb the delayed sum.

nodes.name: Global finite length implies local
nodes.statement: We first show that \cref{global_finite} implies \cref{local_finite}. Indeed, recall from \eqref{eq:local_diff}: \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\|. \end{align*} Therefore, summing for $t=0, 1, \cdots, n$ gives \begin{align*} \sum_{t=0}^n \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{t=0}^n \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \\ &\leq (2s+1) \sum_{t=0}^n \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|. \end{align*} The claim then follows by letting $n$ tend to infinity.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce local finite length to global finite length via the local increment bound.

nodes.name: Recall local increment bound
nodes.statement: Indeed, recall from \eqref{eq:local_diff}: \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Local increments are bounded by windowed global increments.

nodes.name: Sum over t
nodes.statement: Therefore, summing for $t=0, 1, \cdots, n$ gives \begin{align*} \sum_{t=0}^n \|\mathbf{x}^i(t+1) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\| &\leq \sum_{t=0}^n \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \\ &\leq (2s+1) \sum_{t=0}^n \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Summing gives a (2s+1) factor.

nodes.name: Let n tend to infinity
nodes.statement: The claim then follows by letting $n$ tend to infinity.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to the limit.

nodes.name: Reduce to global finite length
nodes.statement: By \Cref{thm:limitcon}, the limit points of $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ and $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ coincide and are critical points of $F$. Thus, the only thing left to prove is the finite length property in \cref{global_finite}. By \Cref{assum:sd} and \Cref{assum:bb}, the objective value $F(\mathbf{x}(t))$ decreases to a finite limit $F^*$.
nodes.statement_short: Limit points are critical; only finite length remains; F(x(t)) decreases to F^*.

nodes.name: Limit point set and prox inequality
nodes.statement: Since $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ is assumed to be bounded, the set of its limit points $\Omega$ is nonempty and compact. Summing \cref{usc} over all $i$ and set $\mathbf{z} \in \Omega$, we obtain \[ g(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) \le g(\mathbf{z}) - \frac{1}{2\eta} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|^2 - \sum_{i=1}^{p}\inner{\nabla_i f(\mathbf{x}^i(t))}{\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: The limit point set Omega is compact; sum the prox inequality with z in Omega.

nodes.name: F is constant on limit points
nodes.statement: Note that $\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t) \to 0$. Also, since $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ is bounded and $\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}^i(t)\to 0$ for all $i$, $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ are all bounded. we then take limsup on both sides and obtain that $\limsup_{t\to\infty} g(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) \le g(\mathbf{z})$. Together with the closedness of $g$ we further obtain that $\lim_{t\to\infty} g(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) = g(\mathbf{z})$. Note that $f$ is continuous, we thus conclude that $\lim_{t\to\infty} F(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) = F(\mathbf{z})$ for all $\mathbf{z}\in \Omega$. Note that $F(\mathbf{x}(t)) \downarrow F^*$. Thus for all $\mathbf{x}^* \in \Omega$, we have $F(\mathbf{x}^*) \equiv F^*$.
nodes.statement_short: Limsup plus closedness give F = F^* on Omega.

nodes.name: Apply KL inequality
nodes.statement: Now fix $\varepsilon > 0$. Since $\Omega$ is compact, for $t$ sufficiently large we have $\mathrm{dist}_{\Omega}(\mathbf{x}(t)) \leq \varepsilon$. We now have all ingredients to apply the K\L\xspace inequality in \Cref{def:KL}: for all sufficiently large $t$, \begin{flalign} \varphi'\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^*\big) \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0}) \ge 1. \end{flalign}
nodes.statement_short: For large t the iterates are near Omega, so the KL inequality applies.

nodes.name: Lyapunov decrease
nodes.statement: Since $\varphi$ is concave, we obtain \begin{flalign} \Delta_{t,t+1} &:= \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^*\big) - \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) - F^*\big) \nonumber\\ &\ge \varphi'\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^*\big) \big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) -F(\mathbf{x}(t+1))\big) \nonumber\\ &\ovset{(i)}{\ge} \frac{\alpha \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t) \|^2}{\mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0})}, \end{flalign} where (i) follows from \Cref{assum:sd} and \cref{uKL}. It is clear that the function $\varphi$ (composed with $F$) serves as a Lyapunov function.
nodes.statement_short: Concavity of phi with sufficient decrease bounds squared increments.

nodes.name: AM-GM split
nodes.statement: Using the elementary inequality $2\sqrt{ab} \le a + b$ we obtain from \cref{Lyapunov} that for $t$ sufficiently large, \begin{flalign*} 2\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \le \tfrac{\delta}{\alpha} \Delta_{t,t+1} + \tfrac{1}{\delta}\mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0}), \end{flalign*} where $\delta > 0$ will be specified later.
nodes.statement_short: Bound increments by Lyapunov differences and subgradient distance.

nodes.name: Sum with subdifferential bound
nodes.statement: Recalling the bound for $\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))$ in \cref{subdiff_bound}, and summing over $t$ from $m$ (sufficiently large) to $n$ gives: \begin{flalign*} 2\sum_{t=m}^{n}&\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \le \sum_{t=m}^{n} \frac{\delta}{\alpha} \Delta_{t, t+1} + \sum_{t=m}^{n} \frac{1}{\delta} \mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0}) \\ &\ovset{(i)}{\le} \frac{\delta}{\alpha} \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(m)) - F^*\big) + \sum_{t=m}^{n} \frac{\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L}{\delta} \sum_{k = (t-2s)_+}^t \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \| \\ &\le \frac{\delta}{\alpha} \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(m)) - F^*\big) + \frac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\delta} \sum_{k=(m-2s)_+}^{m-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \| \\ &\qquad\qquad \qquad\qquad + \frac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\delta} \sum_{t=m}^{n} \| \mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t) \|, \end{flalign*} where (i) is due to \cref{subdiff_bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over t using the uniform subdifferential bound.

nodes.name: Choose delta and rearrange
nodes.statement: Setting $\delta = (2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)$ and rearranging gives \begin{flalign*} \sum_{t=m}^{n}\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| &\le \frac{(2s+1)(\sqrt{p}/\eta + 2L)}{\alpha} \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(m)) - F^*\big) \\ &\quad+ \sum_{k=(m-2s)_+}^{m-1} \| \mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|. \end{flalign*}
nodes.statement_short: Choose delta to absorb the right-hand sum.

nodes.name: Conclude finite length
nodes.statement: Since the right-hand side is finite, let $n$ tend to infinity completes the proof for \cref{global_finite}.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded partial sums give finite length.

nodes.name: Uniformized KL inequality along iterates
nodes.statement: \varphi'\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^*\big) \cdot \mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0}) \ge 1.
nodes.label: uKL

nodes.name: Lyapunov decrease
nodes.statement: \Delta_{t,t+1} &:= \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^*\big) - \varphi\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) - F^*\big) \nonumber\\ &\ge \varphi'\big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) - F^*\big) \big(F(\mathbf{x}(t)) -F(\mathbf{x}(t+1))\big) \nonumber\\ &\ovset{(i)}{\ge} \frac{\alpha \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t) \|^2}{\mathrm{dist}_{\partial F(\mathbf{x}(t))}(\mathbf{0})},
nodes.label: Lyapunov

nodes.name: All machines always update
nodes.statement: $\forall i = 1, \cdots, p, \forall t, t \in T_i.$

nodes.name: Proximal Lipschitz property
nodes.statement: We say a pair of functions $f$ and $g$ satisfy the proximal Lipschitz property on a sequence $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ if for all $\eta$ sufficiently small, there exists $L_\eta \in o(1)$, {i.e.}\xspace $L_\eta \to 0$ as $\eta \to 0$, such that for all large $t$, \begin{align} \| \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}(t)) - \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}(t+1)) \| \le L_\eta \|\mathbf{x}(t) - \mathbf{x}(t+1)\|, \end{align} where\footnote{Should the proximal map be multi-valued, we contend with any single-valued selection.} $\Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) \in \prox{g}(\mathbf{x} - \eta\nabla f(\mathbf{x})) - \mathbf{x}$.
nodes.statement_short: The prox-gradient displacement Delta_eta is Lipschitz along the sequence with constant L_eta -> 0 as eta -> 0.
nodes.label: assum:EL

nodes.name: Proof of proximal Lipschitz for smooth g
nodes.statement:
Let us denote $L_f$ and $L_g$ as the Lipschitz constant of the gradient $
abla f$ and $
abla g$, respectively. Since $\Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) \in \prox{g}(\mathbf{x} - \eta 
abla f(\mathbf{x})) - \mathbf{x}$, using the optimality condition for the proximal map, see for instance \cite[Proposition 7(iii)]{YuZMX15}, we have $$ \mathbf{x} + \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) + \eta 
abla g ig(\mathbf{x} + \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) ig) = \mathbf{x} - \eta 
abla f(\mathbf{x}), $$ and similarly $$ \mathbf{z} + \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{z}) + \eta 
abla g ig(\mathbf{z} + \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{z}) ig) = \mathbf{z} - \eta 
abla f(\mathbf{z}). $$ Subtracting one inequality from another, we obtain  egin{align*} \|\Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) - \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{z})\| &= \|\eta 
abla g ig(\mathbf{z} + \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{z}) ig) - \eta 
abla g ig(\mathbf{x} + \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) ig) + \eta 
abla f(\mathbf{z}) - \eta 
abla f(\mathbf{x})\| \ &\leq \eta L_g \| \mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x} + \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{z}) - \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) \| + \eta L_f \|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}\| \ &\leq \eta L_g \| \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{z}) - \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) \| + \eta (L_f+L_g) \|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{x}\|. \end{align*} Rearranging we obtain $$ \|\Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) - \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{z})\| \leq  rac{\eta(L_f+L_g)}{1-\eta L_g} \|\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x}\|, $$ when $0 < \eta < 1/L_g$. Clearly, when $\eta$ is mall, the leading coefficient $	frac{\eta(L_f+L_g)}{1-\eta L_g} \in \mathcal{O}(\eta) \subseteq o(1)$, and our proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Use the prox optimality equation for smooth g, subtract at two points and rearrange to get an O(eta) Lipschitz constant.

nodes.name: Subtract and bound
nodes.statement:
Subtracting one inequality from another, we obtain  egin{align*} \|\Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) - \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{z})\| &= \|\eta 
abla g ig(\mathbf{z} + \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{z}) ig) - \eta 
abla g ig(\mathbf{x} + \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) ig) + \eta 
abla f(\mathbf{z}) - \eta

nodes.name: Rearrange and conclude
nodes.statement: Rearranging we obtain $$ \|\Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}) - \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{z})\| \leq \frac{\eta(L_f+L_g)}{1-\eta L_g} \|\mathbf{z}-\mathbf{x}\|, $$ when $0 < \eta < 1/L_g$. Clearly, when $\eta$ is mall, the leading coefficient $\tfrac{\eta(L_f+L_g)}{1-\eta L_g} \in \mathcal{O}(\eta) \subseteq o(1)$, and our proof is complete.

nodes.name: Finite length without sufficient decrease assumption
nodes.statement: Let \Cref{assum:bb,assum:smooth,assum:separable,assum:delay,assum:always} hold for \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace, and let $F$ satisfy the K\L\xspace property in \Cref{def:KL}. Fix any $r > 1$ with $C = \tfrac{r^{s+1}-1}{r-1}$ and step size $\eta$ such that $\eta < \frac{1}{L(1+2\sqrt{p}C+2\sqrt{p}s)}$. If for each local sequence $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}$ generated by \textsf{m-PAPG}\xspace, \Cref{assum:EL} holds with $L_\eta \leq \frac{r^2-1}{2pr^2C^2}$, and the global sequence $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ is bounded, then the finite length properties in \eqref{global_finite} and \eqref{local_finite} hold. In particular, $\{\mathbf{x}(t)\}$ and $\{\mathbf{x}^i(t)\}_{i=1}^p$ converge to the same critical point of $F$.

nodes.name: Proof of finite length under proximal Lipschitz
nodes.statement:
Using the elementary inequality $\|a\|^2 - \|b\|^2 \le 2\|a\|\|a - b\|$, we have for all $t$:  egin{flalign} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - &\mathbf{x}(t)\|^2 - \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1)ight\|^2 
onumber\ &\le 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \left\|(\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)) - (\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1))ight\| 
onumber\ &\leq 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \sum_{i=1}^{p}\left\|(x_i(t+1) - x_i(t)) - (x_i(t+2) - x_i(t+1))ight\|
onumber\ &\ovset{(i)}{\leq} 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \sum_{i=1}^{p} \left \|\Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}^{i} (t)) - \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}^{i} (t+1))ight\|
onumber\ &\ovset{(ii)}{\le} 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \left(\sum_{i=1}^{p} L_\eta \|\mathbf{x}^{i} (t) - \mathbf{x}^{i} (t+1)\| ight)
onumber\ &\ovset{(iii)}{\le} 2pL_\eta \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\|, \end{flalign} where (i) is due to \Cref{assum:always} hence $t\in T_i$ for all $t$, (ii) follows from \Cref{assum:EL}, and (iii) is due to \eqref{eq:local_diff}. If for some $r > 1$ there exists some $T$ such that for all $t \geq T$,  egin{align} \sum_{k=( t-s)_+}^{ t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \ge C \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|, \end{align} where $C= rac{r^{s+1}-1}{r-1} > s+1$ (since $r > 1$ and w.l.o.g. $s > 0$). Summing the index $t$ from $T$ to $n$ yields  egin{flalign} C\sum_{t= T}^{n}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| &\leq \sum_{t=T}^{n}\sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t}\left\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)ight\|
onumber\ &\leq (s+1)\sum_{t=(T-s)_+}^{n}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\|,
onumber \end{flalign} which after rearranging terms becomes  egin{flalign} (C - s - 1)\sum_{t= T}^{n}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \leq (s+1)\sum_{t=(T-s)_+}^{T-1}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\|. 
onumber \end{flalign} Since the right hand side does not depend on $n$, letting $n$ tend to infinity we conclude  egin{flalign} \sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|< \infty, \end{flalign} and the proof of the finite length property would be complete. Therefore, in the remaining part of the proof, we can assume \eqref{eq:case} fails for infinitely many $t$. Take any such $t=\hat t$, we have  egin{align} \sum_{k=( t-s)_+}^{ t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \leq C \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \leq C^2 \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|, \end{align} since $C > 1$. Combining \eqref{eq:induction} and \eqref{eq:induction2} we have for $t=\hat t$:  egin{flalign} \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\|^2 - \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1)ight\|^2 &\le 2pL_\eta C^2 \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\|^2 
onumber\ &\leq \left(1- rac{1}{r^2} ight) \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\|^2,
onumber \end{flalign} if $\eta$ is small enough (recall that $L_\eta = o(1)$). After rearranging terms we conclude that for $t=\hat t$:  egin{align} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \le r\|\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1)\|. \end{align} Using induction we can continue the same process for any $t \geq \hat t$. Indeed, suppose \eqref{eq:ind} is true for any $t \leq m-1$, then \eqref{eq:induction} holds (for any $t$), and \eqref{eq:induction2} also holds: If $m \leq \hat t + s$, then  egin{align*} \sum_{k=(m-s)_+}^{m}\!\!\! \|\mathbf{x}(k\!+\!1) \!-\! \mathbf{x}(k)\| &= \sum_{k=(m-s)_+}^{\hat t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| + \sum_{k=\hat t+1}^{m}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \ &\ovset{(i)}{\leq} \sum_{k=(\hat t-s)_+}^{\hat t} \!\! \|\mathbf{x}(k\!+\!1) \!-\! \mathbf{x}(k)\| + \sum_{k=\hat t+1}^{m} \!\!r^{m-k} \|\mathbf{x}(m\!+\!1) \!-\! \mathbf{x}(m)\| \ &\ovset{(ii)}{\leq} C\left[\|\mathbf{x}(\hat t+1) - \mathbf{x}(\hat t)\| + \sum_{k=\hat t+1}^{m} r^{m-k} \|\mathbf{x}(m+1) - \mathbf{x}(m)\|ight] \ &\ovset{(iii)}{\leq} C \sum_{k=\hat t}^{m} r^{m-k} \|\mathbf{x}(m+1) - \mathbf{x}(m)\| \ &\ovset{(iv)}{\leq} C^2 \|\mathbf{x}(m+1) - \mathbf{x}(m)\|, \end{align*} where (i) is due to the induction hypothesis, (ii) is due to the definition of $\hat t$ and the fact that $C>1$, (iii) is due to again the induction hypothesis, and finally (iv) is due to the definition of $C$ (recall $m\leq \hat t +s$). If $m > \hat t + s$, the same inequality, with $C^2$ replaced by $C$, would still hold (essentially dropping all the first terms on the right hand side of the above inequalities). Thus, \eqref{eq:induction} and \eqref{eq:induction2} would imply again \eqref{eq:ind} for $t = m$. Lastly, we recall from \cref{eq: func_moment} that for large $t$,  egin{flalign} F ig(\mathbf{x}(t+1) ig) - F ig(\mathbf{x}(t) ig) &\le 	frac{1}{2}(L - 1/\eta) \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|^2 
onumber\ &\quad+ \sqrt{p}L\|\mathbf{x}(t+1)-\mathbf{x}(t)\| \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t-1} \|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k) \|. 
onumber \ &\leq 	frac{1}{2}(L - 1/\eta) \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|^2 + \sqrt{p}CL\|\mathbf{x}(t+1)-\mathbf{x}(t)\|^2. 
onumber \ &\leq -\alpha \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|^2, 
onumber \end{flalign} where $\alpha = 	frac{1}{2}(1/\eta - L - 2\sqrt{p}CL) > 0$ if $\eta$ is small. Hence, the sufficient decrease property in \Cref{assum:sd} is verified and the finite length properties follow from \Cref{thm:finite}.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on whether windowed increments dominate the current one; otherwise induction shows increments shrink geometrically slowly, yielding sufficient decrease and Theorem Finite Length.

nodes.name: Bound change of squared increments
nodes.statement:
Using the elementary inequality $\|a\|^2 - \|b\|^2 \le 2\|a\|\|a - b\|$, we have for all $t$:  egin{flalign} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - &\mathbf{x}(t)\|^2 - \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1)ight\|^2 
onumber\ &\le 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \left\|(\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)) - (\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1))ight\| 
onumber\ &\leq 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \sum_{i=1}^{p}\left\|(x_i(t+1) - x_i(t)) - (x_i(t+2) - x_i(t+1))ight\|
onumber\ &\ovset{(i)}{\leq} 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \sum_{i=1}^{p} \left \|\Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}^{i} (t)) - \Delta_\eta(\mathbf{x}^{i} (t+1))ight\|
onumber\ &\ovset{(ii)}{\le} 2\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \left(\sum_{i=1}^{p} L_\eta \|\mathbf{x}^{i} (t) - \mathbf{x}^{i} (t+1)\| ight)
onumber\ &\ovset{(iii)}{\le} 2pL_\eta \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \cdot \sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\|, \end{flalign} where (i) is due to \Cref{assum:always} hence $t\in T_i$ for all $t$, (ii) follows from \Cref{assum:EL}, and (iii) is due to \eqref{eq:local_diff}.
nodes.statement_short: Proximal Lipschitz and local increment bound control consecutive squared increments.

nodes.name: Case: windowed sums dominate
nodes.statement:
If for some $r > 1$ there exists some $T$ such that for all $t \geq T$,  egin{align} \sum_{k=( t-s)_+}^{ t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \ge C \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|, \end{align} where $C= rac{r^{s+1}-1}{r-1} > s+1$ (since $r > 1$ and w.l.o.g. $s > 0$). Summing the index $t$ from $T$ to $n$ yields  egin{flalign} C\sum_{t= T}^{n}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| &\leq \sum_{t=T}^{n}\sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t}\left\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)ight\|
onumber\ &\leq (s+1)\sum_{t=(T-s)_+}^{n}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\|,
onumber \end{flalign} which after rearranging terms becomes  egin{flalign} (C - s - 1)\sum_{t= T}^{n}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \leq (s+1)\sum_{t=(T-s)_+}^{T-1}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\|. 
onumber \end{flalign} Since the right hand side does not depend on $n$, letting $n$ tend to infinity we conclude  egin{flalign} \sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|< \infty, \end{flalign} and the proof of the finite length property would be complete.
nodes.statement_short: If (63) eventually always holds, increments are summable directly.

nodes.name: Case hypothesis
nodes.statement: If for some $r > 1$ there exists some $T$ such that for all $t \geq T$, \begin{align} \sum_{k=( t-s)_+}^{ t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \ge C \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|, \end{align} where $C=\frac{r^{s+1}-1}{r-1} > s+1$ (since $r > 1$ and w.l.o.g. $s > 0$).
nodes.statement_short: Assume the windowed sum dominates C times the increment for all t >= T.

nodes.name: Sum and rearrange
nodes.statement:
Summing the index $t$ from $T$ to $n$ yields  egin{flalign} C\sum_{t= T}^{n}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| &\leq \sum_{t=T}^{n}\sum_{k=(t-s)_+}^{t}\left\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)ight\|
onumber\ &\leq (s+1)\sum_{t=(T-s)_+}^{n}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\|,
onumber \end{flalign} which after rearranging terms becomes  egin{flalign} (C - s - 1)\sum_{t= T}^{n}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\| \leq (s+1)\sum_{t=(T-s)_+}^{T-1}\left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)ight\|. 
onumber \end{flalign}
nodes.statement_short: Summing gives (C-s-1) times the tail sum bounded by a fixed sum.

nodes.name: Finite length in this case
nodes.statement: Since the right hand side does not depend on $n$, letting $n$ tend to infinity we conclude \begin{flalign} \sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|< \infty, \end{flalign} and the proof of the finite length property would be complete.
nodes.statement_short: Let n go to infinity.

nodes.name: Case: (63) fails infinitely often
nodes.statement: Therefore, in the remaining part of the proof, we can assume \eqref{eq:case} fails for infinitely many $t$. Take any such $t=\hat t$, we have \begin{align} \sum_{k=( t-s)_+}^{ t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \leq C \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \leq C^2 \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|, \end{align} since $C > 1$. Combining \eqref{eq:induction} and \eqref{eq:induction2} we have for $t=\hat t$: \begin{flalign} \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\right\|^2 - \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1)\right\|^2 &\le 2pL_\eta C^2 \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\right\|^2 \nonumber\\ &\leq \left(1-\frac{1}{r^2} \right) \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\right\|^2,\nonumber \end{flalign} if $\eta$ is small enough (recall that $L_\eta = o(1)$). After rearranging terms we conclude that for $t=\hat t$: \begin{align} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \le r\|\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1)\|. \end{align} Using induction we can continue the same process for any $t \geq \hat t$. Indeed, suppose \eqref{eq:ind} is true for any $t \leq m-1$, then \eqref{eq:induction} holds (for any $t$), and \eqref{eq:induction2} also holds: If $m \leq \hat t + s$, then \begin{align*} \sum_{k=(m-s)_+}^{m}\!\!\! \|\mathbf{x}(k\!+\!1) \!-\! \mathbf{x}(k)\| &= \sum_{k=(m-s)_+}^{\hat t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| + \sum_{k=\hat t+1}^{m}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \\ &\ovset{(i)}{\leq} \sum_{k=(\hat t-s)_+}^{\hat t} \!\! \|\mathbf{x}(k\!+\!1) \!-\! \mathbf{x}(k)\| + \sum_{k=\hat t+1}^{m} \!\!r^{m-k} \|\mathbf{x}(m\!+\!1) \!-\! \mathbf{x}(m)\| \\ &\ovset{(ii)}{\leq} C\left[\|\mathbf{x}(\hat t+1) - \mathbf{x}(\hat t)\| + \sum_{k=\hat t+1}^{m} r^{m-k} \|\mathbf{x}(m+1) - \mathbf{x}(m)\|\right] \\ &\ovset{(iii)}{\leq} C \sum_{k=\hat t}^{m} r^{m-k} \|\mathbf{x}(m+1) - \mathbf{x}(m)\| \\ &\ovset{(iv)}{\leq} C^2 \|\mathbf{x}(m+1) - \mathbf{x}(m)\|, \end{align*} where (i) is due to the induction hypothesis, (ii) is due to the definition of $\hat t$ and the fact that $C>1$, (iii) is due to again the induction hypothesis, and finally (iv) is due to the definition of $C$ (recall $m\leq \hat t +s$). If $m > \hat t + s$, the same inequality, with $C^2$ replaced by $C$, would still hold (essentially dropping all the first terms on the right hand side of the above inequalities). Thus, \eqref{eq:induction} and \eqref{eq:induction2} would imply again \eqref{eq:ind} for $t = m$.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise, increments satisfy a reverse growth bound from some time on, proved by induction.

nodes.name: Case hypothesis at t-hat
nodes.statement: Therefore, in the remaining part of the proof, we can assume \eqref{eq:case} fails for infinitely many $t$. Take any such $t=\hat t$, we have \begin{align} \sum_{k=( t-s)_+}^{ t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \leq C \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \leq C^2 \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\|, \end{align} since $C > 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Take t-hat where (63) fails; windowed sum <= C^2 times current increment.

nodes.name: Combine at t-hat
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:induction} and \eqref{eq:induction2} we have for $t=\hat t$: \begin{flalign} \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\right\|^2 - \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1)\right\|^2 &\le 2pL_\eta C^2 \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\right\|^2 \nonumber\\ &\leq \left(1-\frac{1}{r^2} \right) \left\|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\right\|^2,\nonumber \end{flalign} if $\eta$ is small enough (recall that $L_\eta = o(1)$).
nodes.statement_short: Small L_eta yields a contraction of squared increments.

nodes.name: Ratio bound
nodes.statement: After rearranging terms we conclude that for $t=\hat t$: \begin{align} \|\mathbf{x}(t+1) - \mathbf{x}(t)\| \le r\|\mathbf{x}(t+2) - \mathbf{x}(t+1)\|. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Increment at t is at most r times the next one.

nodes.name: Induction over t
nodes.statement: Using induction we can continue the same process for any $t \geq \hat t$. Indeed, suppose \eqref{eq:ind} is true for any $t \leq m-1$, then \eqref{eq:induction} holds (for any $t$), and \eqref{eq:induction2} also holds: If $m \leq \hat t + s$, then \begin{align*} \sum_{k=(m-s)_+}^{m}\!\!\! \|\mathbf{x}(k\!+\!1) \!-\! \mathbf{x}(k)\| &= \sum_{k=(m-s)_+}^{\hat t}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| + \sum_{k=\hat t+1}^{m}\|\mathbf{x}(k+1) - \mathbf{x}(k)\| \\ &\ovset{(i)}{\leq} \sum_{k=(\hat t-s)_+}^{\hat t} \!\! \|\mathbf{x}(k\!+\!1) \!-\! \mathbf{x}(k)\| + \sum_{k=\hat t+1}^{m} \!\!r^{m-k} \|\mathbf{x}(m\!+\!1) \!-\! \mathbf{x}(m)\| \\ &\ovset{(ii)}{\leq} C\left[\|\mathbf{x}(\hat t+1) - \mathbf{x}(\hat t)\| + \sum_{k=\hat t+1}^{m} r^{m-k} \|\mathbf{x}(m+1) - \mathbf{x}(m)\|\right] \\ &\ovset{(iii)}{\leq} C \sum_{k=\hat t}^{m} r^{m-k} \|\mathbf{x}(m+1) - \mathbf{x}(m)\| \\ &\ovset{(iv)}{\leq} C^2 \|\mathbf{x}(m+1) - \mathbf{x}(m)\|, \end{align*} where (i) is due to the induction hypothesis, (ii) is due to the definition of $\hat t$ and the fact that $C>1$, (iii) is due to again the induction hypothesis, and finally (iv) is due to the definition of $C$ (recall $m\leq \hat t +s$). If $m > \hat t + s$, the same inequality, with $C^2$ replaced by $C$, would still hold (essentially dropping all the first terms on the right hand side of the above inequalities). Thus, \eqref{eq:induction} and \eqref{eq:induction2} would imply again \eqref{eq:ind} for $t = m$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction propagates the windowed bound and the ratio bound to all t >= t-hat.
